title: Best-effort runtime state seeding can still abort when reading existing state fails
reasoning: The helper is documented as best-effort and catches failures from set_current_system_state, but it calls get_current_system_state without the same protection. If an agent implementation exposes a callable getter that raises because its runtime state store is unavailable or transiently invalid, the exception escapes before the setter try/except and can fail query execution instead of merely skipping state seeding.
recommendation: Wrap the getter call in the same best-effort error handling used for the setter, log the failure, and proceed with only the incoming runtime_state or skip applying state if that is the intended invariant.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover input shaping, stream state, completion event forwarding, and cancellation reconciliation, but none exercise apply_query_runtime_system_state or a failing get_current_system_state path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend unit test for apply_query_runtime_system_state with an agent whose get_current_system_state raises and set_current_system_state records whether incoming runtime state is still applied or safely skipped, according to the chosen contract.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/services/query_execution_support/query_execution_runtime.py plus a focused backend test for runtime state getter failure handling.
